hints.storageEnabled: You hold the vendor's stock and ship from your own warehouse. Turn this off and vendors can only book you for pickups. At least one of the two models must stay on.
hints.monthlyStorageFee: Charged per distinct product you hold, every month. Set 500 → a vendor storing 40 SKUs is billed 20,000 XAF a month.
hints.pickPackFee: Charged once per order you pick and pack, whatever its size. Set 300 → 50 orders in a month bills 15,000 XAF.
hints.localDeliveryFee: Your fee for a delivery inside a region you cover. Set 1,500 and each local order earns 1,500 XAF, before the delivering agent's share.
hints.outOfRegionDeliveryFee: Replaces the local fee when the drop-off falls outside your coverage regions. Set 3,000 and a Douala → Bafoussam order bills 3,000 instead of the local rate.
hints.pickupEnabled: The vendor keeps its own stock and you collect per order, priced by weight. At least one of the two models must stay on.
hints.baseRateFirstKg: Covers the first kilogram of any pickup. Set 1,000 → a 0.4 kg parcel still bills 1,000 XAF.
hints.additionalPerKg: Added for every kilogram past the first. With a 1,000 base and 250 here, a 4 kg parcel bills 1,000 + 3 × 250 = 1,750 XAF.
hints.outOfRegionSurcharge: Added on top of the weight price when the drop-off falls outside your coverage regions. Set 2,000 and that 4 kg parcel bills 3,750 XAF.
hints.codFeeType: Percentage bills a share of the order value; Fixed bills a flat amount. Changing the type re-reads the value beside it — 2 means 2% under Percentage, and 2 XAF under Fixed.
hints.codFeeValue: Your fee for collecting and remitting the cash. At Percentage 2, a 50,000 XAF COD order earns you 1,000 XAF.
hints.failedDeliveryFee: Charged when the agent reaches the customer but the handover fails — nobody home, or refused at the door. Set 500 and each failed attempt still bills 500 XAF.
hints.rtoFee: Charged when a shipment goes back to the vendor undelivered. It replaces the delivery fee for that shipment — you earn the RTO fee instead of it, not on top of it.
hints.peakSeasonSurcharge: A flat amount added to each order during periods you declare busy. Leave it at 0 to never surcharge.
hints.pricingNotes: Free text shown to vendors alongside your rates. Use it for anything the fields above can't express — volume discounts, fragile-goods handling.
hints.codEnabled: Whether you accept cash-on-delivery orders at all. Off, and vendors can only route prepaid orders to you. This is separate from the COD handling fee above, which prices the ones you do accept.
hints.codMaxAmount: Orders worth more than this are never offered to you as COD. Leave it empty for no cap; set 200,000 and a 250,000 XAF cart has to be prepaid.
hints.returnsPayer: Who is billed for the return trip. "Vendor" deducts it from the vendor, "Agency" means you absorb it, "Customer" bills it at collection.
hints.returnsHandlingFee: Your fee for processing a return once it is back with you. Set 1,000 and each returned order bills 1,000 XAF on top of the return trip itself.
hints.returnsWindowDays: How long after delivery a return can still be raised. Set 7 → an order delivered on the 1st can be returned until the 8th; on the 9th it is refused.
hints.returnsNotes: Conditions the fields above can't express, shown to vendors before they connect. E.g. "only unopened items, original seal intact".
hints.damageClaimDeadline: How long after delivery a damage claim can still be filed against you. Set 7 and a claim raised on day 8 is out of time.
hints.damageMaxRefund: Caps what you pay out per damaged item, whatever the item is worth. Set 50,000 and a 200,000 XAF item still settles at 50,000.
hints.damageNotes: What you require before accepting a claim — photos, original packaging, an unboxing video.

events.title: Events
events.description: Pick which events trigger a notification.
events.shipmentAssignedDescription: When a vendor dispatches an order to your agency.
events.connectionUpdatedDescription: Requests, approvals, rejections and reapproval prompts from vendors.
events.contractUpdatedDescription: When an agent applies to deliver for you, answers an offer you sent, proposes a change to a contract they hold, or counters the terms.
events.contractUpdatedCaveat: A proposed change to a live contract does nothing until you answer it — your agreed terms keep applying meanwhile.
events.payoutUpdatesDescription: When your payout request is created, paid or rejected.
events.codDepositUpdatesDescription: Agent hand-over declarations you must answer, and direct-to-platform payments.
events.codDepositUpdatesCaveat: Turning this off does not stop the 2-day clock — an unanswered declaration still freezes your rolling-reserve releases.
events.planUpdatesDescription: When your subscription plan is nearing expiry, has expired, or you cross your shipment cap.
events.storageAlertDescription: When your media storage passes 80%, 90% or 100% of your plan's limit.
